research_metadata.research_title: Kalaburagi Rural Business Feasibility Study - Mini Toor Dal Processing and Packaging Unit
research_metadata.business_name_input: Mini Toor Dal Processing and Packaging Unit

business_profile.business_name: Mini Toor Dal Processing and Packaging Unit
business_profile.sub_category: Pulse Milling and Processing - Toor Dal
business_profile.business_model: Micro manufacturing + Packaging + Local wholesale and retail
business_profile.description: Procurement of raw toor (red gram) from local farmers and APMC mandis in Kalaburagi district, cleaning, dehusking, splitting, polishing and grading into toor dal, and packaging in 1kg, 5kg, 25kg bags for sale to local retailers, wholesalers, kirana stores, hotels and institutional buyers. Kalaburagi is the largest producer of toor dal in Karnataka and known as Tur Bowl, with GI-tagged Gulbarga Tur Dal.

rural_suitability.reason: Kalaburagi district accounts for ~3.7 lakh hectares of red gram cultivation, 60% of Karnataka production and 70% of district agri land under tur. Raw material locally available in all four target taluks (Aland, Afzalpur, Jewargi, Kalaburagi). GI tag provides premium positioning.

pricing_model.pricing_method: Raw toor cost + milling conversion (72-75% recovery) + processing cost + margin
pricing_model.example_calculation: Raw cost Rs 65/kg / 0.73 recovery = Rs 89/kg base + Rs 12 processing + Rs 8 packaging + Rs 10 margin = Rs 119/kg selling price

taluk_comparison.recommendation_reason: Kalaburagi taluk has highest demand score (830k population, 541k urban), best market access (NH50, railway, APMC main yard), high input arrival from all taluks, and GI branding advantage. Despite high competition, gap exists for branded GI packaged dal. Jewargi is second best due to APMC Jewargi everyday tur trading providing excellent procurement and local sale. Afzalpur weakest due to smallest population 220k and lower urban infrastructure though still feasible.

seasonality.peak_period: October to February - Post Kharif harvest arrival peak, raw price low, milling peak
seasonality.low_period: May to July - Lean raw availability, price high, demand stable but procurement cost up
seasonality.reason: Toor is Kharif crop harvested Oct-Jan in Kalaburagi. Raw arrival high in APMC in these months. Festival season Oct-Nov and Jan increases dal demand.
seasonality.business_impact: Revenue higher in peak due to lower raw cost and higher volume. Lean period margin squeezes but can be managed with storage.
mitigation: Procure and store raw during peak season for lean season milling
Maintain 2-3 months raw buffer stock in ventilated godown
Offer 5% advance booking discount to farmers in sowing season
Diversify into moong, chana milling in off-season using same machinery

climate_factors: Drought - Kalaburagi is semi-arid, rainfall variability affects tur yield
Excess rainfall during harvest affects grain quality
climate_and_climate_change.climate_change_risk: Medium - IMD data shows Kalaburagi stations potential evapotranspiration high, rainfall variability increasing, tur yield sensitive to prolonged dry spells
climate_and_climate_change.business_impact: Drought year reduces local raw availability and raises price by 15-25%. Excess rain at harvest increases broken percentage.
mitigation_measures: Source from multiple taluks not single village
Build covered storage with moisture control
Use moisture meter and keep below 12%
Crop insurance link via farmer tie-up
adaptation_strategy: Flexible pricing formula linked to APMC modal price
Multi-pulse milling capability to switch to chana if toor scarce
sources: IMD district forecast, NABARD climate notes, UAS Raichur

assumptions.source: Market price range 5830-6700 per quintal reported 2025, MSP 6000
Kalgudi mini dal mill output efficiency 72-75% for Toor

financial_model.calculation_methodology: Monthly Revenue = Dal output kg per day * Working days * Selling price + By-product sales. Dal output = Raw kg per day * Recovery %. Expenses = Raw cost + Labour + Electricity + Rent + Packaging + Transport + Maintenance + Misc. Based on NABARD per mill investment ranges and TradeIndia machinery costs.

risk_analysis.financial_risk: Medium - Working capital intensive, price rise in lean season

strengths: Kalaburagi is Tur Bowl of Karnataka - 3.75 lakh hectares under tur, 60% of state production, raw material at doorstep
GI-tagged Gulbarga Tur Dal awarded 14 Aug 2019 valid till 25 Sep 2027 - premium branding opportunity unique to district
Simple technology mini dal mill processes all pulses toor, moong, urad, chana with 72-75% recovery for toor
High daily staple demand - 830k population in Kalaburagi taluk, 342k Aland, 296k Jewargi, 220k Afzalpur ensures recurring demand
weaknesses: Low margin business - raw cost 75-80% of selling price, sensitive to price volatility
Working capital heavy - need to hold 2-3 months raw stock
Electricity dependent - 10-25 HP needed, rural power fluctuations
Quality variation - broken recovery 1-3% if conditioning not proper
opportunities: PMFME 35% subsidy up to Rs 10 lakh plus Karnataka additional 15% (total 50%) for micro food processing - verified via PIB and Karnataka State presentation
Branded GI packaging gap - most mills sell loose, opportunity for FSSAI branded 1kg packs and e-commerce via India Post Bhima Pulses model
Export potential to Hyderabad, Mumbai, Solapur where Gulbarga dal known for high calcium and potassium due to basalt black soil
Multi-pulse utilization - same machinery can mill chana, moong in off-season, increasing capacity utilization
threats: Import of cheap African toor crashing local prices to Rs 3500-3700 vs MSP 6000 causing farmer distress and supply chain disruption
Large automated mills in Kalaburagi industrial area with economies of scale
Climate - drought in Kalaburagi semi-arid zone reduces yield
MSP procurement delays pushing farmers to distress sale and price manipulation by traders

seven_day_validation_experiment.objective: Validate raw availability, customer willingness to pay for GI branded packed dal, and supplier quotes in target taluk before investing

days.target: Visit APMC Kalaburagi main yard, Taj Sultanpur, and nearest taluk APMC (Jewargi/Aland/Afzalpur). Count active dal mills, note their selling price loose vs packed, note raw toor modal price.
days.measurement: At least 5 mills visited, price list collected, raw price range documented

days.target: Interview 20 potential customers: 10 households, 5 kirana shops, 2 hotels, 2 hostel mess, 1 wholesale trader. Ask current dal source, price paid, willingness to pay premium for GI-tagged packed dal, preferred pack size.
days.measurement: 15+ interviews, note average price paid, 60%+ interested in branded pack

days.target: Contact 3 machinery suppliers (TradeIndia list 1.8-3.95 lakh range), get written quotes for mini dal mill. Contact 5 farmers/traders for raw toor supply commitment and credit period.
days.measurement: 3 machinery quotes, 3 farmer supply commitments, credit terms

days.target: Buy 50 kg raw toor, get it milled on job-work basis at existing mill, test recovery %, polishing quality, packaging in 1kg pouches with dummy label.
days.measurement: Recovery % measured (target 72-75%), packaging cost per kg, quality feedback from 5 customers

days.target: Try to sell 50 kg packed dal to kirana shops and households at Rs 110-120/kg. Collect advance orders for next month.
days.measurement: Number of kg sold, number of pre-orders, customer acquisition cost, rejection reasons

days.target: Calculate actual per kg economics from Day 4-5 data: raw cost, milling charge, packaging, transport, profit margin. Compare with financial model assumptions.
days.measurement: Per kg profit, break-even volume per day, monthly profit projection

days.activity: Decision - Proceed / Modify / Do Not Proceed
days.target: Review all data: if >10 customers interested, margin > Rs 8/kg, raw availability assured for 3 months, proceed. If margin low but demand high, modify to job-work model initially. If no demand or raw price too volatile, do not proceed.
days.measurement: Decision document with evidence, next steps, investment plan

success_criteria: At least 15 customer interviews with 60% showing interest in GI branded pack
Raw toor availability confirmed from 3 suppliers within 20km
Machinery quote under Rs 4 lakh for 1 TPD
Sold 30+ kg in test sales at target price
failure_criteria: Raw price > Rs 75/kg making margin negative
No machinery service in Kalaburagi district
seven_day_validation_experiment.decision_rule: Proceed if success criteria 5/6 met and margin positive. Modify to job-work or trading model if demand high but capital insufficient. Do Not Proceed if raw unavailable or margin negative consistently.

government_schemes.scheme_selection_method: Select the five most relevant currently applicable schemes based on verified business eligibility and financial relevance.

capital_and_financing.recommended_funding_pathway: Start with Small Scale 0.5 TPD under PMFME: Own contribution 10% Rs 1.75 lakh + PMFME subsidy 35% up to Rs 10 lakh (Centre) + Karnataka top-up 15% + Bank loan under CGTMSE collateral free. For women entrepreneur, use PMEGP 35% rural special category subsidy (own 5%) or Stand-Up India 10 lakh to 1 crore collateral free. Use MUDRA Tarun for working capital. Register Udyam and FSSAI first, then apply via DIC Kalaburagi District Level Committee via pmfme.mofpi.gov.in portal.

final_feasibility.strongest_reason_to_consider: Kalaburagi district is Tur Bowl of Karnataka with 3.75 lakh hectares under tur, 60% state production, GI-tagged Gulbarga Tur Dal (GI awarded 14 Aug 2019) with premium due to calcium/potassium rich basalt black soil, daily staple demand, and APMC Kalaburagi largest arrival hub. Mini dal mill recovery 72-75% with machinery cost 1.8-3.95 lakh makes micro enterprise viable. PMFME 35% + Karnataka 15% total 50% subsidy significantly reduces capital risk.
final_feasibility.biggest_risk: Raw price volatility - market price Rs 5830-6700 vs MSP Rs 6000 and distress price Rs 3500-3700 due to African import, plus drought in semi-arid zone affecting yield. Mitigation via peak season bulk procurement and multi-pulse milling.
final_feasibility.minimum_viable_startup: Small scale 0.5 TPD with Rs 14.5 lakh total investment, Rs 3.5 lakh working capital, break-even 18 months expected, monthly profit expected Rs 80k. Can start even as job-work milling for farmers to reduce raw inventory risk.
final_feasibility.recommended_scale_for_beginner: Small Scale 0.5 TPD rented shed in Kalaburagi taluk near APMC or Jewargi APMC area - lowest risk, test market with GI branded 1kg packs
final_feasibility.recommended_validation_before_investment: Execute 7-day validation: APMC visits, 20 customer interviews, machinery quotes, 50kg job-work milling test, actual 30kg sales, unit economics calculation
final_feasibility.loan_readiness: High - PMFME, PMEGP, MUDRA, Stand-Up all support dal mill, collateral free up to Rs 10 lakh via CGTMSE, women entrepreneurs 69% MUDRA and 84% Stand-Up beneficiaries
final_feasibility.overall_data_confidence: Medium - Strong verified data on production, GI tag, APMC presence, scheme subsidy, population. Taluk-level competitor counts and exact investment figures estimated due to incomplete public Udyam taluk database.

major_data_gaps: Taluk-level exact number of dal mills not available in public Udyam database - Udyam does not expose taluk-level search without paid access
Exact APMC distance km for each taluk needs field verification
Real-time raw toor price changes daily - need live APMC modal price
Machinery exact landed cost in Kalaburagi including installation and GST
